cleanIntro:
The SLH762 is one of SIG's SL Series rifle cans, covered by SIG's SL Series operator's manual. That book names the series, not each model. It is a sealed can: SIG does not authorize taking it apart and says SL Series cans need no internal cleaning. The job is outside work only: the can's threads, its body, and the threads it mounts on.

The book describes two ways an SL can mounts. A QD can has a locking collar and threads onto a SIG muzzle base. A direct-thread can screws straight onto the barrel and has wrench flats. Follow the steps for the mount yours has. SIG sets the interval at a minimum of every 500 cartridges.

This guide follows SIG's SL Series suppressors operator's manual (P/N 8101692-01 REV 02), which covers the series as a whole. Check your can against that book.

steps.title: Host unloaded, chamber seen and felt empty
steps.action: Before you touch the can, clear the rifle it is on by that rifle's own procedure: magazine out, action open, and the chamber both looked into and checked with a finger. SIG asks for both, not one or the other. Taking a can off puts your hands at the muzzle, so the host is empty first.
steps.quote: ALWAYS ENSURE THE FIREARM IS UNLOADED AND CLEARED BY VISUALLY AND PHYSICALLY INSPECTING THE CHAMBER PRIOR TO INSTALLING, TIGHTENING, OR REMOVING A SUPPRESSOR.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 3.1 ATTACHING SUPPRESSOR, WARNING UNLOAD/CLEAR, printed p.17

steps.title: Let it cool before you reach for it
steps.action: Wait until the can is cold to the touch. A rifle can stays hot well after the handguard feels fine, and SIG warns that touching it hot can burn unprotected skin badly. Leave it on the rifle, muzzle in a safe direction, until it has cooled.
steps.caution: Never touch the suppressor when hot.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 4.0 REMOVING SUPPRESSOR FROM FIREARM, WARNING HOT SURFACE, printed p.27

steps.title: QD can: collar to the unlock icon
steps.action: On a QD can, turn the locking collar until the indicator dot lines up with the unlock icon. You should hear a click. Turn the collar only to unlock it. Turning it to try to take the can off locks it instead.
steps.caution: Do not attempt to remove the suppressor by turning collar.
steps.aside: There should be an audible click.
steps.quote: Unlock the suppressor from the base by rotating the locking collar to align the indicator dot with the unlock icon.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 4.1 REMOVING QD MOUNTED SUPPRESSOR FROM MUZZLE BASE, step 1, printed p.28

steps.title: QD can: turn the whole can counterclockwise off the base
steps.action: With the collar unlocked, grip the can body and turn it counterclockwise until it comes off the muzzle base. The base and brake stay on the barrel. If the can will not turn, carbon has locked it to the base: hold the rifle so it cannot twist, and use a strap wrench or SIG's optional SL Accessory Wrench to break it loose.
steps.aside: Use either a strap wrench or the optional SL Accessory Wrench to loosen the suppressor from the muzzle base.
steps.quote: Rotate the suppressor counterclockwise and remove it from the base.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 4.1 REMOVING QD MOUNTED SUPPRESSOR FROM MUZZLE BASE, step 2, printed p.28

steps.title: Direct-thread can: rifle held, wrench on the flats
steps.action: On a direct-thread can, hold the rifle so it cannot twist, then put a wrench on the can's wrench flats to break it loose from the barrel. SIG gives the sizes: 13/16 inch for a 5.56 can, 7/8 inch for a 7.62 or .300BLK can. Once it breaks loose, unthread it by hand.
steps.aside: For 5.56 suppressors, use a 13/16 inch wrench. For 7.62 and 300BLK suppressors, use a 7/8 inch wrench.
steps.quote: Use an appropriate wrench to loosen the suppressor from the barrel.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 4.3 REMOVING A DIRECT THREAD SL SERIES SUPPRESSOR, step 2, printed p.29

steps.title: The can stays sealed
steps.action: With the can off the rifle, the strip is done. SIG does not authorize taking the can apart. There are no end caps or baffles for you to remove, and the maintenance chapter opens with that warning. Everything below is done to the outside of the can and to the threads.
steps.quote: DISASSEMBLY OF THE SUPPRESSOR IS NOT AUTHORIZED.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.0 MAINTENANCE, CAUTION, printed p.30

steps.title: Ventilation, eye protection, the solvent's own label
steps.action: Work somewhere with good airflow and wear eye protection before any solvent comes out. Read the warnings on the solvent or cleaner you are about to use. SIG points you to the solvent maker's label, not its own book.
steps.quote: USE IN A WELL-VENTILATED AREA. WEAR EYE PROTECTION.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.4 CLEANING, WARNING CLEANING, printed p.30

steps.title: Clean the can's threads
steps.action: Clean the residue out of the can's mounting threads, using a nylon brush for carbon. Never use steel: a steel wire brush damages the Cerakote finish. Clean threads let the can seat fully and come off again next time.
steps.aside: USE A NYLON BRUSH FOR REMOVING CARBON BUILDUP.
steps.quote: Clean the suppressor threads of any residue buildup.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.4 CLEANING, step 1, printed p.31

steps.title: Wipe the body with CLP, then dry
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the can with a rag dampened with CLP to lift the residue, then wipe it dry. Use a light touch: SIG warns against over-lubricating, and solvents can harm the finish.
steps.quote: Wipe the suppressor body with a rag moistened with CLP to remove any residue.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.4 CLEANING, step 2, printed p.31

steps.title: Barrel threads with a brush and dry solvent, no lube on the base
steps.action: Brush the residue off the threads the can mounts on, using a dry cleaning solvent (SIG names one like MIL-P-D-680). Keep CLP and every other lubricant off the muzzle base. Carbon between the can and the muzzle makes the can harder to remove each time, so a can that is getting hard to remove means the base needs cleaning more often.
steps.caution: Do not use CLP or any other lubricant on the muzzle base.
steps.quote: Clean any residue buildup from the barrel threads with a brush and a dry cleaning solvent
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.4 CLEANING, step 3, printed p.31

steps.title: Nothing goes inside
steps.action: Do not clean the inside of the can. SIG says SL Series cans need no internal cleaning. Do not put water, oil, grease, or anything else into the can, and do not soak it. The book forbids adding any substance to the inside.
steps.caution: Do not add any substance such as water, oil, grease, or wire pulling gel into the suppressor.
steps.quote: SL series suppressors do not require any internal cleaning.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.4 CLEANING, NOTE, printed p.30

steps.title: QD can: dull a polished locking surface, check the collar moves freely
steps.action: On a QD can, look at the locking surface. If it has gone shiny and highly polished, dull it with an abrasive cloth. Then work the locking collar between locked and unlocked: it must move freely both ways. Check the muzzle base threads, the collar threads and the brake for damage while you are there.
steps.aside: Ensure the locking collar (5) moves freely between the locked and unlocked positions.
steps.quote: Inspect the locking surface (2) for a highly polished appearance.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.5 INSPECTION, step 2, printed p.32

steps.title: Body checked for damage
steps.action: Look over the whole can body for dents, cracks or other damage, and look at the end cap for marks left by a bullet. A can that is damaged, or that you think is damaged, goes back to SIG customer service for repair, not back on the rifle.
steps.quote: Inspect the suppressor body (4) for damage.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER SL Series Suppressors — Operator's Manual — P/N 8101692-01 REV 02 — printed on the back page — 5.5 INSPECTION, step 4, printed p.32

deepAbsentReason: There is nothing below this. SIG's maintenance chapter for the SL Series opens with "DISASSEMBLY OF THE SUPPRESSOR IS NOT AUTHORIZED." and says SL series cans do not require any internal cleaning (printed p.30). Its cleaning procedure (printed p.31) covers the can's threads, its body and the barrel threads, and its inspection (printed p.32) is external. The book prints no teardown to quote.

cleaning.name: SUPPRESSOR THREADS
tasks: Residue cleaned out of the can's mounting threads with a nylon brush
⛔ Never use a steel wire brush on this can: it damages the Cerakote finish

cleaning.name: SUPPRESSOR BODY
tasks: Body wiped with a rag dampened with CLP, then wiped dry
Light touch with CLP: do not over-lubricate, and keep harsh solvents off the finish

cleaning.name: BARREL THREADS AND MUZZLE BASE
tasks: Barrel threads brushed clean with a dry cleaning solvent
⛔ Do not use CLP or any other lubricant on the muzzle base
A can that is getting harder to remove means the base needs cleaning more often

cleaning.name: INSIDE THE CAN
tasks: No internal cleaning: SIG says SL Series cans do not need it
⛔ Never put water, oil, grease or wire pulling gel inside the can

cleaning.name: ⛔ THE SCHEDULE IS THE MAINTENANCE
tasks: Clean and lube at a minimum of every 500 cartridges, sooner with dirtier ammunition
Discoloured baffles are a sign the can has been run too hot

reassembly: Threads first: the can's threads and the threads it mounts on are clean. On a SIG tapered barrel, the tapered locking surface is clean and free of residue too.

QD can: turn the locking collar so the indicator dot lines up with the unlock icon. Thread the can clockwise onto the muzzle base, about two and a half turns, until it is fully seated on the taper. Look at the back of the can: no muzzle base threads should show.
QD can: lock it by turning the locking collar until the indicator dot lines up with the lock icon. You should hear a click.
Direct-thread can: thread it clockwise onto the barrel by hand, then tighten it to 15-20 ft-lbf with a torque wrench: 13/16 inch for a 5.56 can, 7/8 inch for a 7.62 or .300BLK can.

Only on a barrel it is meant for: SIG warns that mounting a can on the wrong barrel can cause serious injury. Bases and direct-thread cans are marked for a 90-degree barrel shoulder or a 25-degree SIG tapered barrel; a 90-degree base on a tapered barrel needs a taper cap.
fncheck: Before firing: look through the can and make sure nothing is inside it. SIG forbids firing through a can with water, debris or anything else in it. A QD can is locked (dot on the lock icon) with no base threads showing; a direct-thread can is torqued. While shooting, check now and then that the can is still tight on the rifle. If accuracy drops suddenly or a bullet hits the target sideways, stop, clear the rifle, and check the can's tightness, the end cap and the body for a baffle strike. If the can is dropped or hit, check it for damage and alignment with the barrel before the next shot.
